What is (E2E) EUCDEX.Ai CONFERENCE?

The Experts 2 Experts EUCDEX.Ai conference (formerly known as E2EVC/ E2EMVC / PubForum) is a global series of non-commercial events within the end user computing community. Our primary objective is to convene top server based computing, virtualization, cloud, onprem and end user computing experts for knowledge exchange and networking. EUCDEX.Ai offers a packed weekend featuring presentations, Master Classes, and discussions led by virtualization vendors' product teams and independent industry experts.

After hosting over 60 successful events, commencing in August 2003 with just 4 participants, E2EMVC has evolved into a renowned event with approximately 200 attendees from over 25 countries. Over the past two decades, our conferences have been held in various cities worldwide, including Athens, London, Copenhagen, Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Brussels, Cape Town, Frankfurt, Dublin, Orlando, Paris, Prague, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Madrid, Montreal, Munich, New York, Nice, Lisbon, Rome, Hamburg, Hong Kong, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Tel Aviv, and Vienna. Each event typically features 40 - 50 sessions covering server, application, desktop, and storage virtualization, showcasing products from industry leaders such as Microsoft, Parallels, VMware, Citrix, and others.

More than 50 virtualization experts from the community share their insights on the industry's current landscape. Many prominent figures in the virtualization sector have participated in our events in the past or continue to do so. The success of this event is attributed to the attendees, presenters, and sponsors who contribute to its success.

Implementing Microsoft Entra Private Access for 1000+ Users: A Real-World Journey (intro session)

 

Discover how Microsoft Entra Private Access revolutionizes secure access to private corporate resources by eliminating traditional VPN complexities with a modern Zero Trust approach. In this session, we will explore:

What is Microsoft Entra Private Access?

Learn the fundamentals of Microsoft’s cloud-delivered secure access solution, its key features such as identity-centric controls, conditional access, multi-factor authentication, and per-app adaptive access that provide seamless and secure connectivity for  remote and on-premises users across hybrid environments.

How to Implement Microsoft Entra Private Access at Scale

Dive into a practical, real-world case study of deploying Entra Private Access in an enterprise with more than 1,000 users. Understand step-by-step how to configure enterprise applications, set up connectors, apply granular access policies, and roll out secure  access without disrupting user productivity.

Lessons Learned and Best Practices

Gain invaluable insights from the implementation journey, including challenges encountered, strategies for effective segmentation and policy enforcement, user adoption tips, and integration with existing Microsoft 365 security frameworks to maximize security  and usability.

Whether you are planning to modernize your network access strategy or looking for proven solutions to secure your private applications, this session will provide a comprehensive roadmap and actionable takeaways to empower your organization’s Zero Trust journey  with Microsoft Entra Private Access.

When Private Equity Hijacks Your IT Budget: How We Escaped a 12K Seat EUC Renewal in 6 Months (intro

 Soaring renewal quotes. Multi-year lock-ins. “All-you-can-eat” licences that leave a bitter aftertaste. Deep-Dive: Mastering Hydra & Nerdio for Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 (intro session)

Deep-Dive: Mastering Hydra & Nerdio for Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 (intro session)

Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) and Windows 365 have matured rapidly, but operational complexity, cost control, and scalability remain major challenges for enterprises.

In this deep-dive session, we will explore how Hydra and Nerdio Manager can be combined to create a highly automated, scalable, and cost-optimized EUC platform on  Azure.

The session goes beyond basic setup and focuses on real-world operational patterns, automation strategies, and architectural decisions used in large-scale  production environments.

Topics covered include:

  • Designing host pool strategies for AVD & Windows 365 (Enterprise & Frontline)
     
  • Advanced image lifecycle management with Hydra
     
  • Intelligent scaling, power management, and cost governance with Nerdio
     
  • Multi-tenant and enterprise governance models
     
  • Handling GPU-accelerated workloads (vGPU, AI, and graphics)
     
  • Common pitfalls, lessons learned, and best practices from real customer deployments
     

Attendees will leave with practical guidance they can apply immediately, whether they manage a single tenant or hundreds of customers.

The Next Wave of AVD and Windows 365 Adoption (intro)

The Next Wave of AVD and Windows 365 Adoption (intro)

The Next Wave of AVD and Windows 365 Adoption (intro)


21 years in End User Computing, and I watched the first AVD and Windows 365 deployments stick to the easy jobs.

Call centres. Task workers. Lightly managed desktops.

Knowledge workers are a different problem. More apps, more dependencies, more user state, and far less tolerance for a slow login.

This session covers what changes when you scale AVD and Windows 365 to that population:

Application delivery and management without rebuilding images every time something changes

User onboarding and profile management at scale

Visibility into performance and user experience across the environment

The operational blockers that stall large deployments, and how people are getting past them

We'll also look at where the platform and the ecosystem around it are heading, and what that means for your next rollout.

Enabling AI Agents to Operate Desktop Applications Like People (intro session)

 Most enterprise workflows run on desktop applications that lack modern APIs, putting them out of reach of AI automation. Amazon WorkSpaces agent access lets AI agents  securely operate these applications through managed virtual desktops and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with no application changes required. In this session we walk through the architecture, demonstrate agents automating workflows such as data entry and  application testing, and show how to monitor and audit agent activity with CloudWatch and CloudTrail.

EUC for the Agentic Enterprise - The Workspace as a Secure Execution Layer for Agentic AI (intro)

EUC for the Agentic Enterprise - The Workspace as a Secure Execution Layer for Agentic AI (intro)

EUC for the Agentic Enterprise - The Workspace as a Secure Execution Layer for Agentic AI (intro)

Enterprises spent years and significant capital building sophisticated EUC and VDI estates. As remote-work patterns normalized, SaaS adoption accelerated, renewal pressures increased, and alternative application and desktop delivery models matured, many organizations  began to reassess the long-term strategic role of those environments.

Agentic AI should force organizations to reassess the value of their existing EUC platforms and the role those platforms can play in the controlled integration of autonomous agents into the enterprise.

This does not remove the need to modernize authentication, migrate appropriate services out of legacy data centers, improve data governance, or address technical debt. In fact, agentic AI makes those modernization efforts more important. But many of the architectural  and operational principles required to run EUC well controlled execution, identity-based access, application entitlement, isolation, policy enforcement, observability, lifecycle management, and operational accountability closely resemble the disciplines enterprises  will need when introducing autonomous software.

At the same time, the EUC ecosystem itself is evolving. Agent identities, managed execution environments, Conditional Access for agents, MCP gateways, Cloud PCs for agents, and AI-specific policy controls are beginning to blur the line between the traditional  user workspace and a governed execution environment for software actors.

This session explores whether mature EUC architecture can provide a practical starting point for secure agentic AI adoption. We will examine what translates well, what does not, and what still needs to be modernized before agents can be introduced safely at  enterprise scale.

Attendees will leave with an understanding of how agentic AI changes familiar EUC assumptions around identity, execution, applications, data, and trust. The session will explore how established EUC design principles may translate into agent governance; where  Citrix, Windows 365, AVD, Horizon, and similar platforms could play a role as controlled execution environments; why legacy applications may keep EUC relevant in an agentic world; and what still has to change across authentication, data governance, DLP, observability,  lifecycle management, and cloud architecture.

Stop Giving AI Agents Your Desktop (intro session)

Stop Giving AI Agents Your Desktop (intro session)

Stop Giving AI Agents Your Desktop (intro session)

The dominant CUA architecture — agent -> VM -> screenshot -> mouse — treats the agent as a very fast remote employee. But remote computing spent three decades building the primitives agents actually need: session brokering, isolation, process and window ownership, input routing, graphics capture, auditing, and human shadowing. This talk reframes MCP as the control plane over session infrastructure, not the runtime itself. Drawing on lessons from building Vedon, an experimental desktop execution stack for computer-use agents, I'll cover multi-session orchestration, browser attachment, agent/human coexistence, and why VDI-style infrastructure — far from being obsolete — may become the substrate agents run on.

Building Your Own Remote Protocol Extensions: A Practical Guide to Plugins and Virtual CH

11:20 - 12:00, ROOM 3,   When I started tracing my family tree, an online record confidently  placed my great-grandmother in Bad Langensalza. The primary sources said  Bad Homburg. A trusted-looking source had hallucinated - and untangling  it took archives, church books, and a lot of cross-checking to decide  which claim deserved confidence.  That is exactly the discipline AI observability demands. As AI grows  from autocomplete into agents that act on our behalf, "the model said  so" is no longer a source. We need provenance - where did this answer  come from? We need confidence - how sure are we, and what would change  our mind? We need negative results - what did we rule out, and why?  In this session I'll use a real family mystery as the narrative spine  and map every genealogy method - citing primary sources, rating  confidence, disproving false positives, respecting data-access rules -  onto the AI observability toolkit you'll need in production. You'll  leave seeing observability not as another dashboard, but as the practice  of knowing how much to trust each claim your system makes.  No Kirchenbuch required - just the question genealogists have asked for  centuries: where does that come from? He is a big fan of anything with an engine, although he has also spent a lot of time playing tennis and scuba diving.

Despite his last name being of Italian origin, he does not speak a single word of Italian... sorry about that! 😄


Gerardo Luján Moltó is an IT specialist with more than a decade of experience in Microsoft infrastructure, virtualization, and End-User Computing. Over the years, he has designed, implemented, and troubleshot enterprise environments based on technologies such as Microsoft RDS, Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, Parallels RAS, VMware, and hyperconverged infrastructures, combining hands-on technical expertise with solution architecture and technical presales. Currently leading Identity & Access initiatives, Gerardo bridges infrastructure, security, and modern workspace technologies. At EUC EUCDEX.Ai, he will share practical insights and real-world experiences from migrating VDI solutions to Parallels. 



AI @Home with hardware you probably can't afford.

15:10 - 15:50, ROOM 2,  Running modern AI workloads locally promises total data privacy, zero API throttling, and the sheer joy of independent compute—provided you don’t look at the bill. While the open-source community often champions lightweight quantization and modest home-lab setups, truly uncompromised local inference and fine-tuning demand serious enterprise-grade silicon, multi-GPU topologies, and infrastructure that pushes residential power circuits to their absolute limit. This 20-minute talk delivers concrete architectural models from sub-$100 single-task hardware and pragmatic consumer setups to high-end multi-GPU workstations and no-limits enterprise silicon where power and budget cease to exist.

From Scripts to Strategy: Scaling Infrastructure as Code for the Enterprise

AVD Hybrid: A bridge to the cloud, or Schrodinger's desktop? (intro session)

15:10 - 15:50, ROOM 3,  Everyone can write Infrastructure as Code. But building it for the enterprise? That’s a different game.

After years of hands-on experience applying IaC and DevOps practices in large-scale organizations, this session cuts through the theory and shares what actually works in the real world. Moving beyond isolated scripts and proof-of-concepts, we’ll explore how  to design IaC that is scalable, maintainable, and ready for enterprise complexity.

You’ll learn how to structure your codebase for growth, implement effective branching strategies, and establish version control practices that support collaboration across teams. We’ll also cover how to scale deployments across environments, avoid common pitfalls,  and turn fragmented automation into a consistent, governed platform.

Whether you're just starting or already working with IaC, this session will help you elevate your approach from “it works” to “it works at scale.”

Walk away with practical insights to transform your IaC projects into enterprise-grade solutions.
